title: just-deliver Workload
description: What a development team declares their workload needs. Teams specify what, not how - sizing, SKUs, security and monitoring settings come from platform mappings and global IT Ops policies.

apiVersion.description: Schema version this definition is written against.

name.description: Workload identifier. Used to generate resource names, so it must be DNS-safe and short enough to survive per-resource prefixes and suffixes.

team.description: Owning team. Drives approval routing and cost attribution.

environment.description: Target environment. The same definition deploys to every environment; the platform mapping adjusts sizing per environment.

container.description: Container runtime spec (SCORE-compatible subset). Health checks, resource limits, and scaling rules come from global policy.

image.description: Fully qualified image reference including tag.

variables.description: Environment variables. Values may reference provisioned resources with ${resource.<type>.<output>}, substituted at deployment time.

requires.description: Infrastructure the workload needs, declared by type only. The platform picks the concrete resource and its configuration.

items.$comment: Overrides must carry a reason. Expressed as anyOf/not rather than draft-07 'dependencies', which NJsonSchema silently ignores.

type.description: Resource type. Must have a corresponding platform mapping - extend this list as mappings are added.

overrides.description: Escape hatch for edge cases the platform mapping does not yet cover. Only fields on the platform's override whitelist are accepted, and overrides do not persist across deployments.

override_reason.description: Why the override is needed. Required whenever overrides are present - this feeds the platform team's review of which mappings need to change.
